exact_missing_items: Expand Glossary.md so it becomes the owner for the stable term list, with longer help entries explaining: why the object exists, how it relates to nearby objects, common misunderstandings, links to related concepts
History and Ledger especially need precise help because they are easy to collapse into one generic past activity concept
lane and worktree need asymmetric help across surfaces: Orchestrator emphasizes lane as operational object; Source Control emphasizes worktree as concrete Git object
legacy tier wording still present in docs is now both a data-model risk and a user-copy/help migration risk

Highest-pressure docs for condensation are `Plans/storage-plan.md`, `Plans/Contracts_V0.md`, `Plans/Models_System.md`, `Plans/Executor_Protocol.md`, `Plans/WorktreeGitImprovement.md`, `Plans/Crosswalk.md`, and `Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md`.
Widget_System.md still splits terminal widgets between widget.terminal_output and widget.agent_terminal
Orchestrator-owned worktree partitioning still exists only as row metadata (owner run/tier) in Source Control docs, not as a canonical grouping/partition contract
widget layouts still need project-scoped keys rather than implicit global layouts for project-heavy surfaces
baseline: canonical starting lane for a package pool
active: currently eligible/in use for live work
suspect: not safe for normal dispatch until examined or restored
retained: intentionally kept after completion/failure for inspection, compare, or delayed cleanup
cleanup_eligible: no longer needed for live execution and may be archived/removed under policy
archived: historical object retained in the model, but not an active live lane
removed: live backing removed; only historical identity and lineage remain
historical: user-facing historical posture rather than dispatchable live posture
gap_candidates.blocking_reason: Concrete Plans/** document requires content reconciliation vs transfer obligation.
